name: Diff_Chain_1
questiontext:
Find the derivative of the following function: \[ y={{CT:0}} \sin^{-1}\left( {{CT:1}} {{CT:2}}^2\right) \]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
In order to solve this problem we will have to use the chain rule \(\frac{df}{dx}=\frac{df}{dg} \cdot\frac{dg}{dx}\)  as follows:

Define \(g({{CT:2}})={{CT:1}}{{CT:3}}\) and \(f({{CT:2}})={{CT:0}} \sin^{-1}\left( g\right)\).

So, \[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle \frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}\left({{CT:0}} \sin^{-1}\left( {{CT:1}} {{CT:2}}^2\right)\right) &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:2}}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{d}{dg}({{CT:0}} \sin^{-1}\left( g\right))\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}({{CT:1}} {{CT:2}}^2) \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{{CT:0}}{ \sqrt{1-g^2}}\cdot {{CT:4}}{{CT:2}} \\ &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle \frac{{{CT:5}}{{CT:2}}}{ \sqrt{1-{{CT:6}}{{CT:7}}}} \end{array}\]

on_true.feedback: To differentiate a function of a function, you must use the chain rule! It is \[\frac{df}{dg} \cdot\frac{dg}{dx}.\]
You appear to have applied the chain rule incorrectly. It is \[\frac{df}{dg} \cdot\frac{dg}{dx}.\]
